summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would create a national anti-corruption agency for the Commonwealth public sector.
The agency would be led by a judge or retired judge as commissioner, with powers like a royal commission to investigate corruption and refer findings for prosecution.
Federal judges are not covered initially, but the bill includes a process to review their inclusion later.
changes: Establishes the Australian National Integrity Commission as an independent anti-corruption body.
Gives the commission royal commission powers to investigate corruption involving the Commonwealth government.
Creates a mandatory reporting requirement for public officials and agency heads to refer corruption issues.
Sets up a Whistleblower Protection Commissioner within the commission.
Subjects the commission to oversight by a parliamentary joint committee and a parliamentary inspector.
Operates alongside a second bill that would create codes of conduct and a standards commissioner for parliamentarians.
summary.affected: Federal politicians, the federal public sector, and private sector businesses regulated by the Commonwealth.
